meta.title: Kerlico: one file that's both your proxy client and server
meta.description: Kerlico is open-source proxy software. It's a single program file that can work as a client or a server, and it supports 30 protocols.
hero.tag: One file. Both ends of your proxy.
hero.sub: Use it on your own Linux machine, or put it on a server for others to connect to.
uses.title: One program, three ways to use it
uses.lead: No separate client and server to install. It's the same file, and it does whatever your config file tells it to.
uses.client: Run it on your Linux machine. It connects your apps to a remote proxy server.
uses.server: Put it on a cloud server so you and your friends can connect your devices to it.
uses.both: On one machine, it takes incoming connections and passes them on.
how.title: How it works
how.lead: Scroll down to follow one visit from start to finish.
how.aria: Diagram: a phone, a computer and a friend's device all connect to Kerlico. Kerlico either goes straight to the internet or hands off to a remote server, and the visit ends at the website.
how.s1: Phones, computers and friends' devices can all connect to the same Kerlico. Everyone uses their own account.
how.s2: It follows the rules you wrote: does this visit go straight to the internet, or through a remote server?
how.s3: A direct visit leaves from this machine. Through a proxy, the website address goes to the remote server exactly as it is. If the remote server can't connect, Kerlico won't quietly switch to a direct connection.
wall.title: 30 protocols supported
wall.lead: If you've used a proxy protocol somewhere else, it's probably here too. Hover over a triangle, or click it, to see what it does.
proto.vless: A very popular proxy protocol today. It works with many different ways of carrying traffic.
proto.vmess: A long-standing proxy protocol. The whole connection is encrypted.
proto.trojan: Its traffic looks much like a normal HTTPS website.
proto.shadowsocks: A lightweight encrypted proxy that's easy to set up.
proto.ss2022: The newer version of Shadowsocks, with newer encryption.
proto.shadowsocksr: An offshoot of Shadowsocks that also disguises traffic.
proto.anytls: Runs over TLS and makes its traffic harder to recognize.
proto.shadowtls: Borrows the TLS handshake of a real website and hides proxy traffic behind it.
proto.snell: The encrypted proxy protocol used by Surge. Simple and efficient.
proto.tuic: A proxy protocol built on QUIC that connects quickly.
proto.hysteria1: Built on QUIC and tuned for poor-quality connections.
proto.hysteria2: The second generation of Hysteria. Its traffic looks like HTTP/3.
proto.shadowquic: Built on QUIC. Its handshake is disguised as a visit to a real website.
proto.mieru: An encrypted proxy protocol that doesn't rely on TLS.
proto.naive: Its traffic looks like a normal browser visiting a website.
proto.trusttunnel: An open-source tunnel protocol from AdGuard, built on HTTP.
proto.sudoku: Encodes data into special patterns so the traffic is harder to recognize.
proto.socks: One of the most common kinds of proxy. Most apps support it.
proto.http: The most basic kind of proxy. Works with browsers and command-line tools.
proto.wireguard: A modern VPN protocol. Fast and easy to set up.
proto.tun: Lets apps with no proxy settings go through Kerlico too. Linux only for now.
proto.ssh: Turns an SSH server you already have into a proxy.
proto.gost-relay: Connects to relay servers set up with GOST.
proto.tor: Goes through the Tor network, with no separate Tor install.
proto.masque: A new-generation tunnel standard built on HTTP/3.
proto.openvpn: Connects to an existing OpenVPN server, with no separate client to install.
proto.tailscale: Joins a Tailscale private network. Tested with a self-hosted Headscale.
proto.easytier: Joins a virtual local network built with EasyTier.
net.title: It can join your private networks too
net.lead: A company VPN or a network you set up at home: Kerlico can join them directly, without installing their own apps.
use.title: See who used how much, at a glance
use.lead: Give different people their own accounts and passwords. Each person's traffic is counted separately.
use.more: Traffic, speeds and visit records stay on your own machine. They aren't sent to anyone.
